claims.claim: For each fixed positive x0 and positive H, a scale 0<h0<=hP can be chosen with ||log(x0)/log(h0)||_infinity < H; coordinate comparison then forces every active label at x0 to have zero slope, placing x0 in K_h0.
K_hj subset int(B_sqrt(hj)) and h_next=min(sqrt(hj),hP) imply K_hj subset B_h_next, including when the hP cap is active.
Starting from K_h0, invariance/global existence plus the next-box containment permits the finite-entry proposition to be applied successively; nesting of plateaux is unnecessary.
The capped square-root sequence reaches hP after N=ceil(log2(|log h0|/|log hP|)) steps when h0<hP, and after zero steps when h0=hP.
claims.proof: With a_j=-log(h_j), a_(j+1)=max(a_j/2,aP); the least n with a0/2^n<=aP is the stated ceiling.

claims.claim: The final plateau is reached by sum_(j=1)^N W_(h_j), a finite bound independent of the realized rate path for each fixed x0.
K_(hP) intersect (c+S) is nonempty compact convex, positive, forward invariant, and absorbing, conditional on predecessor plateau invariance and class preservation.
The entire all-endotactic permanence theorem is correct or externally validated.

counterexample_search: No counterexample found to the scale lift under its stated predecessor premises.
quantifier_limit: The bound is finite and rate-path-independent for each x0; it is not shown uniform over x0 in an unbounded class.
